data.long_meaning: Doralia is a Latin feminine name which means 'Doris of the sea'. Doris is derived from the ancient Greek Dorida, which is thought to mean 'gift of the sea'. In Greek mythology, Doris was a sea nymph who bore the god Hephaestus a son named Achelous. Thus, Doralia can be seen as a name with both maritime and divine associations, making it a beautiful choice for a Christian girl's name.

historical_references.reference: Dorothea of Caesarea, a renowned Christian saint, was born in the 3rd century in Caesarea (modern day Israel). She is commonly referred to as Dorothea of Caesarea or Saint Dorothea. She was a noblewoman who, despite her wealth and social status, devoted her life to caring for the sick and poor. She was killed during the Roman persecutions of Christians, around 311 AD, for refusing to marry a Roman soldier.

The name Doralia was also used in the 16th century in connection with Dorothea of Montauk, a Danish princess. She was the daughter of King Christian II of Denmark and Queen Isabella of Austria. Her name, Doralia, was given to a Danish colony established in South America, now known as Brazil, as part of her dowry when she was married to Alonso de Mendoza, the Spanish governor of the Spanish colony of Santa Catalina de Monte Cristi in the Caribbean. The name Doralia was used to designate the new colony.
